title: bee close: a blocking uat door under uat_stop close
action: REVISION after a NEEDS_REVISION semantic-judge verdict. Six of seven must_have truths PASS and stay passing — the door is absent under merge and off (proved live), it does reach the blocking enforcement chain in close_handler, the uat-deferral escape mirrors judge-debt exactly, and the diff added no deletions. Truth 4 FAILED: the two ends of the road classify the lane from DIFFERENT sources. The close-time door asks feature_route (which prefers route.lane), while the merge side asks the lane record's mode. Those two disagree on 12 of 95 real records in .bee/lanes — the judge's worked example is .bee/lanes/knowledge-loop.json, which carries mode standard with route.lane small, and bee close --feature knowledge-loop --dry-run emits no judge-debt door, proving feature_route returned small where the merge side reads standard. Under uat_stop close that means close_the_lane_on_merge sets waiting_on gate 'uat: <feature>' while bee close reports the same feature exempt and never blocks: the uat stop disappears silently, which is the exact failure this feature exists to prevent. FIX: there must be ONE lane-classification read for the uat stop, living in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/uat.rs beside uat_gate_applies_to_lane, and both ends must call it. The merge side is canonical — the must_have truth itself says 'the same lane rule the merge side uses' — so lift the merge-side mode read into crate::uat as a named function (something like uat_lane_mode(main_root, feature) -> Option<String>, returning the record's mode with the merge side's exact fallback behavior) and have the close door feed uat_gate_applies_to_lane from it instead of from feature_route. Do NOT change the merge side's behavior and do NOT change what feature_route returns for any other door — judge-debt and every other consumer keep reading it exactly as they do today. Then close the test gap that hid this: the existing exempt-lane test at close.rs writes a lane record carrying only mode and no route, the one shape where the two sources cannot disagree. At least one new test must write a lane record whose mode and route.lane DISAGREE (mode standard, route.lane small) and assert the uat door still blocks under uat_stop close — plus its mirror, mode small with route.lane standard, asserting the door stays exempt.
verify: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml close && PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml uat
done_when: bee close carries a uat door that exists only under uat_stop close; it blocks a standard or high-risk feature whose uat gate is unapproved, passes once approved, is exempt for tiny, small, docs, and spike, is cleared by a uat-deferral decision, and reports an invalid-config detail rather than guessing on a bogus value. Every other door is untouched and the close suite is green.
notes: Phase 2. Depends on usp-1's crate::uat. Files are disjoint from usp-2 — the two run concurrently.

truths: The uat door does not appear at all under uat_stop merge or off.
Under close it blocks a standard or high-risk feature whose uat gate is unapproved.
Under close it passes once the uat gate is approved.
Under close it is exempt for tiny, small, docs, and spike, the same lane rule the merge side uses.
A uat-deferral decision naming the feature clears it, mirroring judge-debt.
A bogus uat_stop value blocks with an invalid-config detail rather than resolving either way.
No other close door changes behavior.

trace.outcome: The close-time uat door and the merge side now classify the lane from one read, crate::uat::uat_lane_mode, so a record whose mode and route.lane disagree can no longer make the uat stop vanish between merge and close.

report.outcome: Revision after NEEDS_REVISION. Lifted the merge side mode classification into crate::uat::uat_lane_mode and pointed the close-time uat door at it, replacing feature_route (which preferred route.lane). Added two tests covering a mode/route.lane disagreement in both directions, including the judge worked example knowledge-loop (mode standard, route.lane small). feature_route itself is untouched and judge-debt still reads it exactly as before.
report.tests: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml close — 147 passed, 0 failed — the close suite owns the uat door this cell changed, and the uat filter (49 passed) covers the lifted policy read

checks.truth: The uat door does not appear at all under uat_stop merge or off.
checks.evidence: close.rs:1355 build_close_report_doors — `Some(crate::uat::UatStop::Merge) | Some(crate::uat::UatStop::Off) => {}` pushes nothing; the door is ABSENT, not merely non-blocking. Live cross-check with the repo's own config (no `uat_stop` key, so uat_stop_config -> Merge): `.bee/bin/bee close --feature uat-stop-placement --dry-run --json` printed doors [tests, scribing-debt, capture-queue, judge-debt, pattern-check, knowledge-freshness, impact, routing, doc-deferral] — no `uat` entry. Unit test close.rs:3398 `uat_door_is_absent_under_merge_and_under_off` asserts the same for default and for `{"uat_stop":"off"}`.

checks.truth: Under close it blocks a standard or high-risk feature whose uat gate is unapproved.
checks.evidence: close.rs:1337 `let uat_blocking = lane_applies && !gate_approved && !uat_deferred;` and close.rs:1339 pushes Door{door:"uat", blocking:uat_blocking}. The door DOES reach the enforcement chain: close.rs:1797 `if doors.iter().any(|d| d.door == "uat" && d.blocking)` returns Out::Emit(..., 1) with CLOSE_UAT_PREFIX (close.rs:67 "Uat gate pending for"), placed after the scribing-debt and judge-debt refusals and before pattern-check. Test close.rs:3521 `close_refuses_the_uat_door_for_a_standard_lane_feature_under_uat_stop_close` drives close_handler end to end and asserts exit code 1. high-risk is not separately tested, but feature_route returns "high-risk" (close.rs:331 FEATURE_ROUTE_LANE_CLASSES) and uat_gate_applies_to_lane(Some("high-risk")) is true (uat.rs:57), so the path is identical.

checks.truth: Under close it passes once the uat gate is approved.
checks.evidence: close.rs:446 `uat_gate_approved` reads the live workflow record's gates.uat.approved first, falling back to .bee/state.json approved_gates.uat ONLY when state.feature == this feature — byte-for-byte the same shape as the merge side's uat_merge_precheck (verbs/worktree/phases.rs:859-895), including the foreign-feature guard. Test close.rs:3435 `uat_door_does_not_block_once_uat_is_approved` asserts blocking:false, detail "clear", command None.

checks.truth: Under close it is exempt for tiny, small, docs, and spike, the same lane rule the merge side uses.
checks.evidence: The PREDICATE is shared (close.rs:1333 calls crate::uat::uat_gate_applies_to_lane, the same fn phases.rs:876 calls), but the INPUT is not. Close classifies via `feature_route` (close.rs:333-359): lane record `route.lane` first, then state.route.lane, then `mode` only if it is one of the six lane classes. Merge classifies via the live workflow record's `mode`, falling back to the lane record's `mode` (phases.rs:865-875). These disagree on 12 of 95 real lane records in .bee/lanes — e.g. .bee/lanes/knowledge-loop.json has mode="standard" but route.lane="small": merge reads standard (applies), close reads small (exempt). Runtime proof of the close-side read: `.bee/bin/bee close --feature knowledge-loop --dry-run --json` emits NO judge-debt door, and judge-debt is built only for feature_route in {standard, high-risk} (close.rs:1250) — so feature_route returned "small" for a lane whose mode is "standard". Consequence under uat_stop="close": phases.rs:499 close_the_lane_on_merge uses uat_merge_precheck and SETS waiting_on gate "uat: knowledge-loop", while bee close then reports the lane exempt and never blocks — the two D4 halves instruct the user in opposite directions. Full list of divergent lanes: doctor-binary-freshness, grooming-round-1, knowledge-loop, merge-commits-the-lane, pocock-nuggets, porting-protocol, test-doctrine-text-sweep, two-flows, wayfinding-craft, wayfinding-triggers, windows-ci-path-fixes, worktree-orphan-verdict (all in the direction merge-applies / close-exempt). Test close.rs:3449 `uat_door_does_not_block_for_exempt_lanes_under_close` writes a lane record carrying ONLY `mode` and no `route`, the one shape where the two sources cannot disagree, so it does not exercise this.

checks.truth: A uat-deferral decision naming the feature clears it, mirroring judge-debt.
checks.evidence: close.rs:423 `has_uat_deferral_decision` is a line-for-line mirror of `has_judge_deferral_decision` (close.rs:405) — active_decisions + filter_decision_events with DecisionFilters{tag:"uat-deferral", feature:<feature>}; same struct and same fields the capture-deferral and judge-deferral escapes already use (decisions/read.rs:313). Consumed at close.rs:1335-1337 so a deferral drops `blocking` to false and the detail reads "deferred — ...". Test close.rs:3494 `uat_door_is_cleared_by_a_logged_uat_deferral_decision` logs a real decisions.jsonl line tagged uat-deferral and also asserts a decision naming a different feature does NOT lift this one.

checks.truth: A bogus uat_stop value blocks with an invalid-config detail rather than resolving either way.
checks.evidence: close.rs:1319-1327 — the `None` arm of uat_stop_config pushes Door{door:"uat", blocking:true} whose detail names both keys and all legal values ("uat_stop" must be "merge", "close", or "off"; the legacy "uat_before_merge" must be a boolean ...). uat.rs:31-46 confirms None is produced by a bogus string, a non-string uat_stop, and a non-boolean uat_before_merge. Test close.rs:3474 `uat_door_blocks_with_invalid_config_detail_on_a_bogus_uat_stop_value` asserts blocking plus every one of those substrings. It reaches the same refusal at close.rs:1797.

checks.truth: No other close door changes behavior.
checks.evidence: `git show ec1717ff --unified=0 -- packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/close.rs` is 290 insertions, 0 deletions across 5 pure-add hunks (@@ -62,0 +63; -412,0 +419; -1255,0 +1307; -1685,0 +1787; -3249,0 +3375) — no existing line was touched, and the doc-deferral door was left alone as instructed. The new Door is named "uat", which collides with no existing `doors.iter().find(|d| d.door == ...)` lookup. `cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml close` printed `142 passed, 1944 filtered out`; `... uat` printed `44 passed, 2042 filtered out`.

semantic_judge.failure_signature: The close-time uat door classifies the lane through feature_route (route.lane first) while the merge side classifies through the record's mode; the two disagree on 12 of 95 real lane records (knowledge-loop: mode=standard, route.lane=small), so under uat_stop=close a merge sets waiting_on gate "uat: <feature>" for a feature bee close then exempts — automatic: the must_have itself names the merge side as canonical, so a follow-up cell can lift that mode read into crate::uat and call it from close with no human decision.

checks.truth: The uat door does not appear at all under uat_stop merge or off.
checks.evidence: close.rs build_close_report_doors: the uat_stop_config match still carries an empty arm for Some(UatStop::Merge) and Some(UatStop::Off) that pushes nothing, so the door is ABSENT and not merely non-blocking. git show 01f29a61 on packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/close.rs touched only the Close arm lane read (all 4 deleted lines sit inside that arm) plus tests, so the Merge and Off arms are byte-identical to the code the prior judge proved live. Test close.rs:3420 uat_door_is_absent_under_merge_and_under_off asserts is_none for the default (no key) and for uat_stop off. I ran cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml uat_door and got 9 passed, 0 failed.

checks.truth: Under close it blocks a standard or high-risk feature whose uat gate is unapproved.
checks.evidence: close.rs:1345 computes uat_blocking as lane_applies and not gate_approved and not uat_deferred, then pushes Door door uat with that blocking flag. The enforcement chain is intact at close.rs:1804, which returns the CLOSE_UAT_PREFIX refusal when any door named uat is blocking. Test close.rs:3437 uat_door_blocks_a_standard_lane_feature_under_close_with_uat_unapproved is green, and the new test at close.rs:3495 also asserts blocking for a mode standard record. Under the new read a high-risk record (mode high-risk) and an unclassifiable one (None) both give uat_gate_applies_to_lane true at uat.rs:58, which exempts only tiny, small, docs and spike, so the blocking path for them is unchanged.

checks.truth: Under close it passes once the uat gate is approved.
checks.evidence: close.rs:446 uat_gate_approved is untouched by 01f29a61. That commit close.rs diff has exactly 3 hunks: the Close arm lane read, the new test helper write_lane_mode_and_route, and two new tests. Test close.rs:3454 uat_door_does_not_block_once_uat_is_approved asserts blocking false, detail clear and command None, and it is green in the 9-test uat_door run.

checks.truth: Under close it is exempt for tiny, small, docs, and spike, the same lane rule the merge side uses.
checks.evidence: The prior defect is closed. close.rs:1339 now reads lane from crate::uat::uat_lane_mode(root, feature), and feature_route is gone from that arm. uat.rs:87-99 uat_lane_mode is expression-identical to the merge side mode read at phases.rs:884-897: I diffed the two blocks (scratchpad/merge_block.txt against scratchpad/uat_block.txt) and the only textual differences are the fn signature versus the let mode binding, plus the trailing let lane_applies line. Same sources, same order, same fallback: list_workflows(main_root).unwrap_or_default(), then find_live_workflow, then wf mode as_str, else read_lane_display(main_root, feature).ok().flatten() and rec mode as_str. Both ends then feed the one predicate uat_gate_applies_to_lane (phases.rs:898 and close.rs:1340). The real record at /home/thanhsmind/projects/goglbe/beehive/.bee/lanes/knowledge-loop.json (mode standard, route.lane small) therefore classifies as standard at BOTH ends, so bee close blocks exactly where close_the_lane_on_merge at phases.rs:502 sets the uat wait. The exempt-lane test at close.rs:3472 (tiny, small, docs, spike) is still green. RESIDUAL, not a truth failure: the merge side keeps its own copy of the mode read instead of calling uat_lane_mode, so the revision brief wording about ONE read that both ends call is met behaviorally but not structurally, and the two copies can drift again.

checks.truth: A uat-deferral decision naming the feature clears it, mirroring judge-debt.
checks.evidence: close.rs:1342-1345 still gates on has_uat_deferral_decision at close.rs:423, the line-for-line mirror of has_judge_deferral_decision at close.rs:405, and the deferred detail branch is unchanged. Commit 01f29a61 touches neither function. Test close.rs:3561 uat_door_is_cleared_by_a_logged_uat_deferral_decision is green in the 9-test uat_door run.

checks.truth: A bogus uat_stop value blocks with an invalid-config detail rather than resolving either way.
checks.evidence: close.rs:1319-1327 keeps the None arm of uat_stop_config pushing a blocking uat door whose detail names both keys and all legal values, and that arm sits OUTSIDE the Close arm the revision edited. uat.rs:30-46 uat_stop_config returns None for a bogus string, a non-string uat_stop and a non-boolean uat_before_merge. Test close.rs:3540 uat_door_blocks_with_invalid_config_detail_on_a_bogus_uat_stop_value is green.

checks.truth: No other close door changes behavior.
checks.evidence: feature_route at close.rs:333-359 is byte-identical, since the 01f29a61 close.rs diff never enters its body. Its only remaining production caller is the judge-debt door at close.rs:1251, which still matches feature_route on standard or high-risk. rg feature_route across packages/bee-rs/crates finds no other call site outside tests and comments. Live cross-check with the shipped binary: bee close --feature knowledge-loop --dry-run --json run from /home/thanhsmind/projects/goglbe/beehive still prints NO judge-debt door for that mode standard, route.lane small record, so feature_route still returns small there, exactly as before the revision. That same fact makes the two new tests falsifying rather than vacuous: against the pre-revision code the door read small for the close.rs:3495 fixture (mode standard, route.lane small) and standard for the close.rs:3519 fixture (mode small, route.lane standard), so each new assertion inverts the old outcome, and the Close arm pushes the door unconditionally, so the if let Some guard in the 3519 test is never skipped. Suites: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml close gave 147 passed, 0 failed, and the same command with filter uat gave 49 passed, 0 failed.
